title: How to buy stocks
subtitle: Your first step into the stock market
openingQuestion: To buy VNM (Vinamilk) shares on HOSE, what's the first thing you need to do?
openingOptions: Go directly to Vinamilk's headquarters to buy shares
Open a trading account at a licensed securities company
Call the State Securities Commission to register a purchase
Wire money directly to the Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange
explanation: Buying stock goes through a mandatory intermediary, a securities company: you open an account, deposit money, place an order, and they route the order to the exchange. There are two things beginners often overlook. First, the real cost includes two-way trading fees plus a tax on the sale value, so more frequent trading erodes more. Second, the settlement cycle: money doesn't arrive right after a sale, so you must plan ahead if you need to spend it.

realWorldExample.description: These are three of the most popular securities companies in Vietnam. You can open an account online in about 10-15 minutes using a chip-based ID card, no branch visit needed. Once approved (usually 1-2 business days), you deposit money into your securities account and can place a buy order right on the mobile app.

quiz.question: How do the HOSE and HNX exchanges differ?
options: HOSE lists stocks, HNX only lists bonds
HOSE trades in the morning, HNX in the afternoon
HOSE is for foreign-owned companies, HNX for domestic ones, a distinction that matters for liquidity
HOSE lists larger companies, HNX smaller and mid-sized ones
quiz.explanation: Vietnam has three main exchanges: HOSE (usually home to large-cap companies like VNM, VCB, FPT), HNX (many smaller and mid-sized companies), and UPCoM (a market for public companies not yet officially listed, usually with lower liquidity).

quiz.question: When placing a buy order, how important is choosing the 'order price'?
options: Very important - setting it below the market price may mean it never matches
Not important, the system automatically matches at the best price for you on either the buy side or the sell side
It only affects the trading fee, not whether the order matches
You must set it exactly equal to that session's ceiling price
quiz.explanation: The stock market matches orders on a best-price, time-priority basis. If you set a buy price lower than what sellers are currently asking, your order will sit and wait, and may never match if the price doesn't fall to that level.

quiz.question: Why must you open an account at a securities company to buy stock?
options: Because the securities company is the one reselling stock it already holds
Because the securities company is an exchange member that places orders on your behalf
Because the law forbids individual investors from owning stock directly
Because you need an account for the issuing company to register you as a shareholder rather than the issuing company directly
quiz.explanation: Only member securities companies can place orders directly on the exchange's system. They're an intermediary: your money and shares are yours, held at the Vietnam Securities Depository, while the securities company just routes orders and collects fees.

quiz.question: How does a limit order (LO) differ from a market order (MP)?
options: LO matches instantly at the best price, MP waits until end of session to match once, the core trade-off between control and certainty
LO is only for buying, MP is only allowed for selling stock
LO fixes the price you accept but may not match; MP matches immediately at the market price
LO and MP are the same thing, just different names between securities companies
quiz.explanation: A limit order gives you control over price: set a buy at VND 30,000 and you'll never pay more, but if no one is selling at that level, the order just sits there. A market order is the opposite - guaranteed to match, but you accept whatever price is currently available, which could be higher than expected during a sharp move.

quiz.question: You want to buy 50 VNM shares on HOSE but the order can't be placed. What is the most likely reason?
options: Because you must buy at least 1,000 shares to qualify as a shareholder
Because VNM only allows institutional investors to buy its shares
Because the quantity ordered must be an even number divisible by 10
Because HOSE trades in 100-share lots, and 50 is an odd lot
quiz.explanation: HOSE matches orders in round lots of 100 shares. To buy fewer, you must use odd-lot trading - usually at a worse price and not always with a counterparty available. This is one reason investors with small capital often choose an ETF or fund certificate instead of collecting individual shares.

quiz.question: After a buy order matches, how long until the shares actually arrive in your account?
options: About two business days, under the T+2 settlement cycle
Immediately, within seconds, like a bank transfer
Exactly 30 days after the order matches on the system
Only once the issuing company confirms and updates the shareholder register
quiz.explanation: Vietnam uses a T+2 settlement cycle: an order matched today means the shares arrive in your account two business days later, and only then can you sell them. This detail often surprises beginners - seeing the price rise the next day but not yet able to lock in the profit.

keyTakeaways: To buy stocks, you must open an account at a licensed securities company - you cannot buy directly from the issuing company
Vietnam has three main exchanges: HOSE, HNX and UPCoM, each with different listing standards
Placing a buy/sell order requires attention to price level and order type (market price, limit price) to understand whether the order will match

practicePrompt.question: You just opened a securities account and want to buy 100 VNM shares trading around VND 70,000. You place a buy order at VND 65,000 to 'buy cheaper'. What is most likely to happen?
options: Your order might not match for the entire session because the price is set much lower than the current market price
The order will definitely match right away because the system always prioritizes matching the lowest-priced buy order to protect the buyer
You'll automatically be filled at 100 shares at VND 70,000 because the system adjusts the order to the current market price
The exchange will reject this order outright because the price gap exceeds the allowed regulatory limit
practicePrompt.explanation: A buy order only matches when a seller accepts that price. Setting a price much lower than the current market price usually means the order doesn't match.

summary.keyIdea: To buy stocks, you must open an account at a licensed securities company - you cannot buy directly from the issuing company
summary.commonMistake: Reading the concept as a phrase to memorize rather than a principle to apply to real decisions.

application.title: Check your own account
application.message: The lesson already has a real example of SSI and VNDirect's fee schedule - see the 'Real example' section above. Now open the app of the securities company you use and check your own account's actual fee schedule against it.
application.secondary: Knowing the fees before placing an order helps you avoid unpleasant surprises later.

sections.text: Many people want to invest in stocks but stop right at the first step because they don't know where to begin. The good news is the process in Vietnam today is much simpler than 10 years ago, and can be done almost entirely online.

You can't buy stock directly - you need a securities company as an intermediary. Vietnam has dozens of licensed securities companies: SSI, VNDirect, HSC (Ho Chi Minh City Securities), VPS, TCBS (Techcom Securities), VCBS... You pick one, register an account online with your chip-based ID card and phone number - this process usually takes 10-15 minutes and is approved within 1-2 business days.
Step 2: Deposit money into the account

Once your account is opened, you transfer money from your bank into the securities account (usually linked directly to a partner bank). This amount shows as 'buying power' on the app, ready to place buy orders.
Step 3: Choose the exchange and ticker

Vietnam has three exchanges: HOSE (Ho Chi Minh City Stock Exchange - home to most large-cap companies like VNM, VCB, FPT, HPG), HNX (Hanoi Stock Exchange - many mid-sized and smaller companies), and UPCoM (a market for public companies not yet eligible for official listing, usually with lower liquidity and higher risk).

items: Each ticker has a 3-letter code: VNM (Vinamilk), FPT (FPT Corp), HPG (Hoa Phat), VCB (Vietcombank)
Trading hours: morning from 9:00 to 11:30, afternoon from 13:00 to 15:00 (weekdays)
Each buy/sell order is usually a minimum of 100 shares (1 round lot) on HOSE
Share prices move within a limited band each session (usually ±7% on HOSE) to prevent overly sharp swings

sections.label: Limit order vs market order
sections.text: Limit order: you set a specific price you want to buy/sell at, and it only matches when someone sells/buys at that price or better. Market order (ATO/ATC in Vietnam): matches immediately at the current market price, prioritizing a fast fill but possibly matching at an undesired price if the market is moving sharply.

After buying, the share price will fluctuate daily. This is a normal part of the market, not a sign you did something wrong. Beginners commonly make the mistake of checking the price constantly and panic-selling when they see a slight dip in the first few days, when stock investing is inherently something to view over cycles of several years.
A real example: SSI and VNDirect's fee schedules

items: SSI: trading fees commonly 0.05%-0.35% of trade value depending on the plan/order channel - self-placed orders through the app are usually lower than through a broker
VNDirect: base trading fee around 0.10%-0.35% of trade value depending on account plan
For a VND 50 million buy order, a 0.15% fee equals VND 75,000 - a small amount but it repeats every trade, so it adds up meaningfully with frequent trading

sections.label: How to check your own account
sections.text: Open your securities company's app, find the 'Fee Schedule' or 'Trading Fees' section under settings/account. A standard Vietnamese securities account can trade on HOSE, HNX and UPCoM all with one account, no need to open separately per exchange.

lines: Opening a securities account at a licensed company is the mandatory first step.
Understanding the exchange, order type, and price band helps you place orders precisely instead of getting confused staring at the price board.
